title: Giant Ancient Snake From India May Have Been One of the Longest Ever
summary:
About 47 million years ago, an enormous snake lived in what is now western India. Scientists say this snake, called Vasuki indicus, may have been one of the largest snakes that ever existed.

The discovery was described in 2024 in the journal Scientific Reports. Paleontologists Debajit Datta and Sunil Bajpai of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee studied fossils found at a mine in Kutch, in the state of Gujarat. They examined 27 fossil vertebrae, the small bones that make up a snake's backbone. Many were well preserved, and some were still joined together. The bones seem to have come from a fully grown snake.

The snake was named after Vasuki, a mythical serpent in Hindu stories that is shown wrapped around the neck of the god Shiva. The word indicus refers to India.

The scientists did not find a whole skeleton. To estimate the snake's size, they compared its bones with the backbones of living snakes. Their estimates ranged from about 36 to 50 feet long. That puts Vasuki in the same range as Titanoboa, a giant snake that lived in what is now Colombia about 60 million years ago and is thought to have reached about 43 feet.

The researchers say their numbers are uncertain, and it is not clear whether Vasuki was really longer than Titanoboa.

The wide backbone bones suggest Vasuki had a thick, heavy body. Scientists think it probably moved slowly. Instead of chasing prey, it may have waited in hiding, much like modern anacondas and pythons. It may have lived on land or in shallow swamps.

At that time, Earth's climate was much warmer than it is today, and the area had wetlands and marshes.
why_it_matters: Fossils like these help scientists understand how Earth's climate and living things have changed, and how some animals once grew far larger than any alive today.

background_read: Fossils form when the remains of a living thing are buried and slowly preserved in rock, letting scientists study animals that lived millions of years ago.
A snake's backbone is made of many vertebrae, so even a few well-preserved bones can help scientists estimate how big the whole animal was.
Snakes are cold-blooded, and scientists think warmer climates in the distant past may have helped some reptiles grow very large.
Titanoboa, found in what is now Colombia, has long been known as one of the largest snakes ever, so new giant snake fossils are often compared with it.
